key_insight: Hurricane Laura’s turbulent inflow strongly changes with LES grid resolution, and those differences materially alter the aeroelastic loads on an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: Accurate extreme-load prediction for wind turbines in tropical cyclone regions requires high-resolution hurricane inflow data, not just coarse wind fields.
method: Large-eddy simulations of Hurricane Laura were run at coarse (55.55 m), intermediate (25 m), and fine (10 m) grid spacing.
The LES outputs were used as direct inflow conditions for aeroelastic turbine simulations.
The study compared mean flow and turbulence structures as the storm passed a virtual turbine location.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant resolution-dependent differences in mean wind and turbulent structures, producing distinct turbine aeroelastic responses.
watch_item: Results depend on the fidelity of the LES inflow and a single storm/path setup, so broader validation across storms and locations is still needed.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
